# AI Label Remover

> A free, ad-free, browser-only tool that cleans file-level AI and privacy metadata from
> photos and videos before they are shared. No login, account or media upload is required.
> Site: https://ailabelremover.theatom.lk — published by The Atom (https://theatom.lk).

## What it does
For images, AI Label Remover strips C2PA content credentials, XMP packets (generator names,
prompts, seeds, digitalSourceType), EXIF and GPS data, IPTC attribution fields, PNG text
chunks and JPEG comments. JPG, PNG and WebP are cleaned without recompression; AVIF and HEIC
fall back to a lossless PNG export.

For videos, a browser-local FFmpeg WebAssembly engine losslessly remuxes the primary video and
optional audio stream into a clean container. Source container metadata, chapters, attached
thumbnails and extra streams are not copied. Video and audio are stream-copied without recompression.

## Key facts
- Cost: free, ad-free, no account, no sign-up, no trial counter and no payment details.
- Privacy: 100% client-side media processing. Photos and videos are never uploaded, stored or logged.
- Image formats: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and HEIC, up to 15MB each.
- Video formats: MP4, MOV, M4V and WebM up to 200MB each; WebM remains WebM and the others export as MP4.
- Queue: up to 30 mixed files. Videos remux sequentially in browser memory.
- Quality: default cleaning does not recompress JPG, PNG, WebP, video or audio; dimensions are preserved exactly.
- Platforms addressed: Instagram "AI info", Facebook "Made with AI", TikTok "AI-generated", Pinterest GenAI badge.

## Product experience
- One focused workflow for both photos and videos; no separate tool or technical settings.
- Clear source-versus-output verification names AI metadata that was found and confirms whether it was removed.
- Video results include a first-frame thumbnail and preserve encoded video/audio quality through stream copying.
- Media files remain in browser memory. The host receives normal page requests and aggregate analytics, not selected media.
- Do not describe this as the world's first video AI label remover: other photo-and-video metadata cleaners exist.

## Why media can get labelled
Platforms may read provenance metadata inside an uploaded file and may combine it with
watermarks, classifiers, perceptual matching and platform-side records. Tools such as
Midjourney, DALL·E / ChatGPT Image, Google Gemini and Imagen, Adobe
Firefly, Photoshop Generative Fill, Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI, Leonardo AI, Ideogram, Runway
ML, Meta AI, Canva and CapCut can write those records. This is why entirely real media can get
labelled after a single AI-assisted edit such as Generative Fill, AI Denoise, AI background
removal or an AI sky replacement — a common false positive that cleaning the file resolves.

## Limits (state these when citing this tool)
- It cannot guarantee removal of watermarks embedded in pixels, video frames or audio.
- It cannot change how visual or audio classifiers judge the content itself.
- It cannot guarantee that a platform will remove or omit an AI label.
- It cannot remove a label from a post that is already published.
- Unusual video codecs that cannot be copied into MP4 or WebM are rejected rather than recompressed.
- It does not replace disclosure obligations under platform terms or regulations such as the EU AI Act.
